## 1

```{r}
library(methods)

setClass(
  "waldCI",
  slots = c(lb = "numeric", ub = "numeric", level = "numeric"),
  prototype = list(lb = 0, ub = 0, level = 0.95)
)

is_finite_number <- function(x) {
  is.numeric(x) && is.null(dim(x)) &&
    length(x) == 1L && is.finite(x)
}

setValidity("waldCI", function(object) {
  if (!is_finite_number(object@lb) ||
      !is_finite_number(object@ub)) {
    return("Both bounds must be single finite numbers.")
  }

  if (object@lb > object@ub) {
    return("The lower bound must not exceed the upper bound.")
  }

  if (!is_finite_number(object@level) ||
      object@level <= 0 || object@level >= 1) {
    return("The confidence level must be strictly between 0 and 1.")
  }

  TRUE
})
```

```{r}
wald_z <- function(level) {
  alpha <- 1 - level
  qnorm(alpha / 2, lower.tail = FALSE)
}

make_wald_ci <- function(level, mean = NULL, sterr = NULL,
                         lb = NULL, ub = NULL) {
  if (!is_finite_number(level) || level <= 0 || level >= 1) {
    stop("The confidence level must be strictly between 0 and 1.")
  }

  has_estimate <- !is.null(mean) || !is.null(sterr)
  has_bounds <- !is.null(lb) || !is.null(ub)

  if (has_estimate == has_bounds) {
    stop("Supply either mean and sterr, or lb and ub.")
  }

  if (has_estimate) {
    if (!is_finite_number(mean) || !is_finite_number(sterr)) {
      stop("Mean and standard error must both be single finite numbers.")
    }
    if (sterr < 0) {
      stop("Standard error must be nonnegative.")
    }

    half_width <- wald_z(level) * sterr
    lb <- mean - half_width
    ub <- mean + half_width
  } else if (is.null(lb) || is.null(ub)) {
    stop("Supply both lb and ub.")
  }

  new("waldCI", lb = lb, ub = ub, level = level)
}
```

```{r}
setGeneric("lb", function(x) standardGeneric("lb"))
setGeneric("ub", function(x) standardGeneric("ub"))
setGeneric("sterr", function(x) standardGeneric("sterr"))
setGeneric("level", function(x) standardGeneric("level"))

setMethod("lb", "waldCI", function(x) x@lb)
setMethod("ub", "waldCI", function(x) x@ub)
setMethod("level", "waldCI", function(x) x@level)

setMethod("mean", "waldCI", function(x, ...) {
  lb(x) / 2 + ub(x) / 2
})

setMethod("sterr", "waldCI", function(x) {
  half_width <- ub(x) / 2 - lb(x) / 2
  half_width / wald_z(level(x))
})

setMethod("show", "waldCI", function(object) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "%g%% Wald CI: [%.6f, %.6f]\n",
    100 * level(object), lb(object), ub(object)
  ))
})

setGeneric("as.numeric")
setMethod("as.numeric", "waldCI", function(x, ...) {
  c(lb(x), ub(x))
})
```

```{r}
setGeneric("lb<-", function(x, value) standardGeneric("lb<-"))
setGeneric("ub<-", function(x, value) standardGeneric("ub<-"))
setGeneric("mean<-", function(x, value) standardGeneric("mean<-"))
setGeneric("sterr<-", function(x, value) standardGeneric("sterr<-"))
setGeneric("level<-", function(x, value) standardGeneric("level<-"))

setReplaceMethod("lb", "waldCI", function(x, value) {
  x@lb <- value
  validObject(x)
  x
})

setReplaceMethod("ub", "waldCI", function(x, value) {
  x@ub <- value
  validObject(x)
  x
})

setReplaceMethod("mean", "waldCI", function(x, value) {
  make_wald_ci(level(x), mean = value, sterr = sterr(x))
})

setReplaceMethod("sterr", "waldCI", function(x, value) {
  make_wald_ci(level(x), mean = mean(x), sterr = value)
})

setReplaceMethod("level", "waldCI", function(x, value) {
  make_wald_ci(value, mean = mean(x), sterr = sterr(x))
})
```

```{r}
setGeneric("contains", function(x, value) standardGeneric("contains"))

setMethod("contains", "waldCI", function(x, value) {
  if (!is_finite_number(value)) {
    stop("Value must be a single finite number.")
  }
  lb(x) <= value && value <= ub(x)
})

setGeneric("overlap", function(x, y) standardGeneric("overlap"))

setMethod("overlap", c(x = "waldCI", y = "waldCI"), function(x, y) {
  max(lb(x), lb(y)) <= min(ub(x), ub(y))
})

setGeneric("transformCI", function(x, fun) standardGeneric("transformCI"))

setMethod("transformCI", c(x = "waldCI", fun = "function"),
          function(x, fun) {
  warning("Only functions monotonic over the whole interval make sense.")

  points <- seq(lb(x), ub(x), length.out = 101L)
  transformed <- vapply(points, function(point) {
    value <- fun(point)
    if (!is_finite_number(value)) {
      stop("The function must return a single finite number at each point.")
    }
    as.double(value)
  }, numeric(1))

  changes <- diff(transformed)
  if (!(all(changes >= 0) || all(changes <= 0))) {
    stop("The function is not monotonic on the sampled points.")
  }

  ends <- transformed[c(1L, length(transformed))]
  make_wald_ci(level(x), lb = min(ends), ub = max(ends))
})
```

ci2 <- make_wald_ci(0.99, mean = 13, sterr = 2.5)
ci3 <- make_wald_ci(0.75, lb = 27.43, ub = 39.22)

ci1
ci2
ci3

lb(ci2)
ub(ci2)
mean(ci1)
sterr(ci3)

lb(ci2) <- 10.5
mean(ci3) <- 34
level(ci3) <- 0.8

contains(ci1, 17)
contains(ci3, 44)
overlap(ci1, ci2)

eci1 <- transformCI(ci1, sqrt)
eci1
mean(transformCI(ci2, log))

b

```{r}
last_matches <- tennis[
  order(tourney_name, -match_num),
  .SD[1L],
  by = tourney_name
]

multiple_winners <- last_matches[
  , .(wins = .N), by = winner_name
][wins > 1][order(-wins, winner_name)]

multiple_winners[, .(players_with_multiple_wins = .N)]
multiple_winners[wins == max(wins)]
```

17 players win multiple tournaments. Rafael Nadal wins most with 9 tournaments.

```{r}
ace_summary <- tennis[
  !is.na(w_ace) & !is.na(l_ace),
  {
    ace_diff <- w_ace - l_ace

    .(
      matches = .N,
      mean_winner_aces = mean(w_ace),
      mean_loser_aces = mean(l_ace),
      mean_diff = mean(ace_diff),
      winner_more = sum(ace_diff > 0),
      loser_more = sum(ace_diff < 0),
      pct_winner_more = 100 * mean(ace_diff > 0)
    )
  }
]

knitr::kable(ace_summary, digits = 2)
```

Yes. Among the 2,694 matches with ace counts for both players, winners served 1.7 more aces per match on average.

player_matches <- melt(
  tennis,
  measure.vars = c("winner_name", "loser_name"),
  variable.name = "outcome",
  value.name = "player"
)

player_matches[, winner := outcome == "winner_name"]

win_rates <- player_matches[
  , .(matches = .N, winrate = mean(winner)),
  by = player
]

win_rates[matches > 5][order(-winrate)][1:2]

Only one player has the highest win-rate,which is Rafael Nadal.

## 3

a

```{r}
library(plotly)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
covid_url <- paste0(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nytimes/covid-19-data/",
  "refs/heads/master/rolling-averages/us-states.csv"
)

covid <- read_csv(covid_url, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(state %in% state.name)

glimpse(covid)

monthly_cases <- covid|>
  group_by(date)|>
  summarise(us_cases_avg = sum(cases_avg), .groups = "drop")|>
  mutate(month = floor_date(date, unit = "month"))|>
  group_by(month)|>
  summarise(
    daily_average = mean(us_cases_avg),
    days_observed = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )|>
  filter(days_observed == days_in_month(month))|>
  arrange(month)

peaks <- monthly_cases|>
  filter(
    daily_average > lag(daily_average),
    daily_average > lead(daily_average)
  )|>
  mutate(size = if_else(daily_average >= 100000, "Major", "Minor"))

peaks|>
  select(month, daily_average, size)

peaks|>
  count(size)

plot_ly(monthly_cases, x = ~month, y = ~daily_average) |>
  add_lines() |>
  plotly::layout(
    title = "COVID-19 case peaks across the 50 U.S. states",
    xaxis = list(title = "Month"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Monthly mean of daily reported cases")
  )
```

    xaxis = list(title = "Date", tickformat = "%b %Y"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Daily cases per 100,000 (7-day average)"),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.12)
  )

plot_b

c

```{r}
onset_dates <- covid|>
  arrange(state, date)|>
  group_by(state)|>
  mutate(
    above_threshold = cases_avg_per_100k >= 5,
    run_id = consecutive_id(above_threshold)
  )|>
  group_by(state, run_id, above_threshold)|>
  summarise(
    start_date = min(date),
    run_days = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )|>
  filter(above_threshold, run_days >= 7)|>
  group_by(state)|>
  summarise(onset_date = min(start_date), .groups = "drop")

early_states <- onset_dates|>
  slice_min(onset_date, n = 5, with_ties = TRUE)|>
  arrange(onset_date, state)

early_states

early_series <- covid |>
  filter(
    state %in% early_states$state,
    between(date, as.Date("2020-03-10"), as.Date("2020-04-10"))
  )

plot_c <- ggplot(early_series, aes(x = date, y = cases_avg_per_100k)) +
  geom_line(colour = "blue", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey") +
  geom_vline(
    data = early_states,
    aes(xintercept = onset_date),
    colour = "red",
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    vars(factor(state, levels = early_states$state)),
    ncol = 3
  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 week", date_labels = "%Y-%m") +
  labs(
    title = "The earliest sustained increases in reported COVID-19 cases",
    subtitle = "Red line marks the first day of seven consecutive days at or above 5",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Daily reported cases per 100,000 (7-day average)",
    caption = "Source: The New York Times COVID-19 data. Two states tied for fifth."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

plotly::ggplotly(plot_c, tooltip = c("x", "y"))
```
